highlights.title: Resident Evil Director Is Already Thinking Sequels
highlights.summary: Weapons director Zach Cregger took a very different approach with his new adaptation of Resident Evil. Rather than adapting the characters and narrative of Capcom's survival-horror game franchise, Cregger is instead translating what it feels like to exist in one of Resident Evil 's worst-case…
body: That may not sound like your typical franchise starter, but a sequel to Resident Evil is already looking likely.

Perhaps the most important indicator that Resident Evil will spawn a sequel is the movie's early box office performance. According to a report from Deadline, September's Resident Evil is already tracking toward a record-setting opening weekend for the franchise — somewhere between $35 million and $50 million domestically. Sony Pictures must be happy about that, considering the previous movie in the franchise, 2021's Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City, finished its theatrical run with a $41.9 million worldwide haul.

Cregger himself might be on board for a sequel. He tells Polygon that he was thinking his Resident Evil journey would be a "one and done" flirtation with Capcom's IP. But after completing the film, he says he has more ideas for the franchise.
In an interview with Cregger, Polygon editor-in-chief Matt Patches asked the director if he was hoping to kickstart the franchise for a possible new trilogy.

highlights.title: Arsenal win with one shot on target as Forest sink into bottom three
highlights.summary: Arsenal's only shot on target proved enough to snatch victory at Nottingham Forest through Noni Madueke's deflected strike, keeping the champions within touching distance of Premier League leaders Manchester City and condemning Forest to the relegation zone.
body: After 80 frustrating minutes at the City Ground, substitute Madueke cut inside from the left and fired towards goal. His strike deflected off Jair Cunha, wrong-footed Matz Sels and found the net to settle a game in which Arsenal had struggled to turn possession into chances.

Arsenal had dominated the ball but registered no shots on target in the first half. Kai Havertz headed wide from a Declan Rice free-kick while Gabriel's set-piece effort was cleared almost off the line by Ousmane Diomande.

Forest made life difficult for Mikel Arteta's side, defending resolutely and threatening on the counter. Murillo almost salvaged a point in stoppage time with a superb solo run, driving at the Arsenal defence before curling narrowly wide. Ezri Konsa then made a crucial late challenge to deny Liam Delap.
However, despite their opportunities, it was the same old story for Oliver Glasner's side, who failed to find a breakthrough.

highlights.title: Don Bradman Cricket Jr Announced for PC and Consoles
highlights.summary: With Cricket 26 developer Big Ant Studios holding somewhat of a monopoly on the cricket videogame genre for more than a decade, fans of the world's second most popular sport have been crying out for some competition within the genre.
body: In comparison, Don Bradman Cricket Jr is arriving eight years late and minus any official team or player licenses, beyond the inclusion of Australia's greatest ever batsman himself as an unlockable character. By completing a specific in-game challenge, players will apparently be able to drop the Don directly into the otherwise entirely generic Australian team, as well as gain access to a bonus minigame that recreates his famous knocking-a-golf-ball-into-a-water-tank-using-a-stump-fo-a-bat training exercise.

Elsewhere, Don Bradman Cricket Jr seems to be offering a fairly basic feature set, with unlicensed tournaments to play and a challenge mode to test your skills with, alongside split-screen support for two players. Not much is known about the actual gameplay, but the developers are promising that the experience of batting will ensure that "no two shots are ever truly the same." This despite the announcement trailer above seeming to show multiple versions of the same pull through mid-wicket.

highlights.title: Supercell brings Clash Royale to tabletop with new Kickstarter board game
highlights.summary: Supercell is bringing Clash Royale to the tabletop with Clash Royale: The Grand Arena, a board game developed with Maestro Media, set to launch on Kickstarter on October 20, 2026.
body: Designed by David Gordon, Ryan Rodriguez, and TAM, the game supports two to four players who can deploy cards, attack opponents and send their towers across two lanes.
Players will compete to destroy towers and collect crowns, the player holding the most crowns in the end wins.

The tabletop adaptation aims to retain several mechanics from the mobile game, including card-based strategy. Players build eight-card decks around a chosen champion, whose evolution card remains with them throughout the game. Players can upgrade or add characters to their decks between battles.

“Clash Royale has earned its place as a leading mobile strategy game by challenging players to think tactically, adapt, and outsmart their opponents,” said Andrea Fasulo, head of licensing at Supercell. “With The Grand Arena, our ambition is to honour that competitive spirit and strategic depth, giving fans a fresh challenge worthy of the game they love.”

highlights.title: Kylie Jenner Debuts on the Victoria’s Secret Runway in its $50 Million Fantasy Bra
highlights.summary: The reality TV star and entrepreneur stepped onto the Victoria's Secret catwalk wearing the most expensive Fantasy Bra to date.
body: For the return of Victoria’s Secret’s pricey and gemstone-encrusted Fantasy Bra—the first time the brand has put it on its runway since 2018—team VS needed a model who is not merely of the moment, but transcends it. They got just that with Kylie Jenner, the reality TV star-turned-beauty entrepreneur, who, with 380 million followers on Instagram, is one of the most popular personalities on the platform. Jenner, 29, stepped out onto the catwalk wearing a gauzy mini skirt, clear heels, and white feathered wings—but it was ultimately the Fantasy Bra that was the center of attention.

To mark its grand return, the brand pulled out all the stops with the bra itself, revealing a design that features 4,410 natural diamonds surrounding a 75.54-carat radiant-cut Fancy Vivid yellow diamond. It took 15 craftspeople more than 1,000 hours to build it, and the finished product weighs just under four pounds. The total cost? A whopping $50 million, the highest price (by some $35 million) for a Fantasy Bra to date.

highlights.title: Don't fall for this - how to protect yourself from AI scams
highlights.summary: Trading standards officers say AI is "super-charging" existing scams through clones and fake websites.
body: Be careful where you buy from, shoppers are being warned as criminals use AI to supercharge scams.
Some fraudsters have made websites for fake retailers that claim to be family-owned firms selling quality UK-made products. Images may show a UK High Street with Union Jack flags in shot.
If you order you're likely to find a product either never arrives, or is a cheap, mass-produced item from a country such as China, trading standards officers say.
AI-generated images like this, as well as voice cloning and deepfake videos are increasingly being used to trick people out of their money, according to National Trading Standards.

highlights.title: OnlyFans Creators Are Pissed That Meta Lets Muse Talk Dirty
highlights.summary: Adult performers are questioning why Meta allows its AI agent to sext while restricting their social media accounts.
body: The generative AI revolution hasn’t been kind to Vanniall, an OnlyFans creator who lives in New York City. She now constantly finds hyperrealistic deepfakes —AI-generated images and videos that copy everything about her— circulating online and often isn’t able to get them removed.

On top of that, Vanniall struggles to build an audience on popular social media platforms, like Instagram, without getting in trouble. “There’s always some sort of report or appeal that I'm going through with them,” she tells WIRED. Vanniall’s Instagram account, which has over 100,000 followers, is currently restricted and cannot be viewed without logging in.

So, when I tell her that Meta allows its AI agent, called Muse, to engage in explicit sexting with adult users, she seems frustrated by the decision: “It's not fair that they get to pull money out of people with their sexually active AI agent, but they won't let real people, real adults, engage in any sort of sensuality or sexuality.”

It’s a common refrain I heard from other adult content creators, who questioned why their accounts on Meta platforms often seem restricted, while Meta’s AI agent is now allowed to talk dirty with millions of adult users.

highlights.title: Ben Simmons’ NBA comeback derailed after tearing achilles tendon in practice
highlights.summary: Sacramento Kings guard to undergo surgery and will miss entire season. Former No 1 draft pick has been attempting to revive his career. Ben Simmons faces a monumental task to revive his NBA career after another devastating injury setback put his comeback attempt with the Sacramento Kings on hold.
body: The 30-year-old signed a one-year deal with the Kings in an attempt to revive his career, but will now miss the entire season. It is another massive setback for the three-time All-Star, after five years battling a series of significant injuries and mental health concerns.

“I’ve faced challenges before that tested me mentally, physically, and emotionally, and I’ve found a way through every single one of them,” Simmons posted in an Instagram story. “This injury is another chapter in my journey, not the end of my story.

“It’s never easy being away from the game I love, especially after everything it took to get back here. But if there’s one thing I’ve learned, it’s that adversity doesn’t define you. How you respond to it does. I’ve been knocked down before, and I’ve always found a way to get back up. This time will be no different.”

highlights.title: Adam Scott's Criminally Overlooked 2026 Thriller Is Finally on Streaming
highlights.summary: You know it's been a good year for horror movies when a genuine hit still slips through the cracks. We spent the summer on discourse over Obsession, The Backrooms, Zach Cregger's Resident Evil, and The End of Oak Street, all of which pulled in nine-digit takes at the box office.
body: What's interesting about the spread in 2026 is that there's room for every type of horror in the current wave. Only a couple of these movies qualify for the old "elevated horror" (read: the real monster is trauma) designation. The rest are good old-fashioned guts-and-gore flicks.
One 2026 hit that is elevated (occasionally literally) is the Irish ghost story Hokum, which debuted in May to rave reviews and solid ticket sales. It made money but wasn’t a blockbuster.

Looking at the year in horror, Hokum managed to thread a very particular sort of needle; it came out two weeks before Obsession and Backrooms went head-to-head at the box office, so it made its money and got out before the real competition started. If you overlooked Hokum in the middle of all that, it's now streaming on Hulu, and it deserves a place in your cinematic rotation in the run-up to Halloween.

Hokum has such a Stephen King-friendly premise that it's a shock to learn he wasn't involved. Instead, Hokum was written and directed by Damian McCarthy, who previously made 2024's Oddity and 2020's Caveat.

highlights.title: A Savannah police officer gave her Flock login to her ICE agent husband
highlights.summary: Now, former Savannah police officer Amber Harpe was fired in August following a department investigation that found she had shared her Flock login information with her husband, Tyler Harpe, an ICE agent.
body: SPD officer Amber Harpe was fired for sharing her Flock access with her ICE agent husband.

While he had unauthorized access to the system, Tyler Harpe conducted 983 searches related to 97 license plates, which were overwhelmingly registered to Hispanic drivers, according to Savannah’s local ABC affiliate, WJCL. The Harpes defended their actions, saying they didn’t use access for personal reasons and that the searches were strictly for “law-enforcement purposes.”

Interim Major Max Nowinsky originally recommended a light eight-hour suspension for Harpe. However, Major Michelle Halford and Assistant Police Chief Robert Gavin disagreed, and they removed her from the force. Harpe was fired, along with five other SPD employees, after an internal investigation uncovered Flock misuse. Four of them were later arrested; however, Harpe was not one of them.

highlights.title: Data Centers Have a New PR Plan: Your Kid’s Field Trip
highlights.summary: Amid a wave of backlash, some industry-friendly groups are employing creative and time-tested strategies to woo the youth.
body: Welcome back to Power Play! Each week, senior writer Molly Taft tackles a topic around this midterm season’s biggest issue: data centers. They’re out this week, so Caroline Haskins is reporting for duty. If you’ve got a question or thought for the column, feel free to shoot Caroline an email at [email protected] or reach her securely on Signal at carolinehaskins.61.

The nonprofit 7x24 Exchange International wants to promote data centers, which they believe are "mission critical” infrastructure. As part of this work, the group recommends a children’s story, “ What is a Data Center?, ” which follows a honey badger named Honey who gets a guided tour of a data center from a worker named Oliver. Oliver explains that the job of data center employees is to make sure that the “functions supported by the data center” are available to anybody, “no matter what time it is.”
"Like when my mom shops online late at night because my dad is sleeping and won't know about it?" Honey asks.

highlights.summary: Festival director Joanna Szymańska-Szcześniak and program director Bartek Pulcyn see more room for growth without the glitz and glam: "Our focus is firmly on the quality of the films."
body: The 42nd edition of the Warsaw International Film Festival is screening 190 films, including 132 features, this year. The Polish fest, which opened Oct. 9 with Jesse Eisenberg ’s The Debut, wraps on Sunday. With 102 world, international or regional premieres, the event offers ample opportunity for discoveries, while also screening highlights from this year’s fest circuit.
How do you see Warsaw’s role, vision and positioning in the annual film festival calendar in Eastern Europe and worldwide?

JOANNA SZYMAŃSKA-SZCZEŚNIAK Warsaw has enormous potential as an international film festival destination. We have a city that is developing rapidly, a strong cultural scene and a festival with more than 40 years of history.

When I became general director, I knew I didn’t want to simply maintain what had already been built. I wanted to give the festival new energy and think seriously about where it should be in five or 10 years. For me, that means strengthening our international partnerships, developing our industry activities and making Warsaw an increasingly attractive destination for filmmakers, producers and audiences.

highlights.title: Mister Organ is one of the most unsettling documentaries I’ve ever seen
highlights.summary: Mister Organ doesn't reach the level of societal horror of The Act of Killing or the creepypasta-meets-true-crime gruesomeness of Beware the Slenderman, but there's something deeply unsettling about Michael Organ and his intimate campaign of terror against everyone who enters his life.
body: The story of Michael Organ is the rare documentary that doubles as a psychological horror film.

Mister Organ is a documentary by David Farrier, an Auckland, New Zealand journalist. The movie starts with Farrier reporting on Bashford Antiques, a shop in Ponsonby that has begun aggressively clamping cars in its lot and demanding exorbitant fees to release them — up to $760. Farrier’s article for The Spinoff eventually led the government to introduce legislation that would outlaw extreme clamping fees.
Under normal circumstances, that would be the end of the story. But at the center of this story is a man named Michael Organ who turns out to be a bizarre, seemingly dangerous conman.

Organ was hired to police Bashford’s lot, and during his investigation, Farrier discovers he’s more than just a parking-lot bully. Years earlier, Organ had been charged with attempting to steal a yacht in an elaborate scheme. What’s more, he claimed to be a prince and a lawyer — he is neither.

highlights.title: Giving AI a “crystal clear” view of the materials world
highlights.summary: New research can help AI models understand crystalline materials in 3D and reason about their properties.
body: In principle, artificial intelligence could make finding the right material for an application as simple as ordering dinner: Scientists would tell a large language model what they want, and it would serve them the perfect material for the job.

Unfortunately, that approach doesn’t work well yet, and the problem comes down to data: Most materials consist of 3D arrangements of crystals, not the text streams that today’s large language models are trained on. The experimental literature is also heavily biased toward a few popular classes of crystals, making AI outputs skew toward those materials.

Now MIT researchers have created a multimodal AI model that tackles these problems. The model combines 3D atomic structures with natural language descriptions to create rich linguistic descriptions about the structures from experimental research papers and first-principles computational databases. The unified description outlines not just the chemical composition and structure, but also its properties, processing considerations, and potential applications, helping AI learn more about what makes materials impactful.

highlights.title: 63 Years Later, the Stellar Action Comic Strip Most America Never Heard of Deserves Another Shot
highlights.summary: This goes double for newspaper comics, which are often viewed as disposable in ways that graphic novels aren't. Surprisingly few of them ever pick up an international audience. Exceptions include Andy Capp and Fred Basset, British strips that have substantially outlived their original creators.
body: One of the cool things about the internet is how it’s become much easier to find obscure comics from all over the world, such as bandes dessinées, science-fiction serials, and stories buried in old magazine anthologies. For every comic that actually gets translated for release outside its original country, such as Valerian or Yoko Tsuno, there are dozens more that don’t. Many of these are long out of print and kept alive online by small communities of fan translators and preservationists. Finding a good one can feel like striking gold.

The British adventure comic Modesty Blaise, created by the late Peter O'Donnell, was virtually unknown in the United States during its original newspaper run, from May 1963 to Feb. 2001. While it has a dedicated audience to this day in much of the rest of the world, over 25 years after it ceased publication, Modesty Blaise was only intermittently carried in American newspapers. This is usually blamed on its frequent nude scenes, which made it too spicy for American audiences. (Modesty is her name, not her practice.) The one exception for years was the Detroit Free Press, and even it censored a couple of strips.

highlights.title: The Most Evocative Period Dramas of the 21st Century
highlights.summary: The best period dramas whisk viewers to times and places that feel a world away from modern life. Here are our favorites, from “Gosford Park” to “The Crown.”
body: Sumptuous costume dramas can provide a much-needed escape in troubling times, but if you’re tired of the usual assortment of airless parlors, manicured lawns, and straight-laced suitors, there is an alternative: a subset of recent films and series that play with our expectations of the genre. Combining post-punk soundtracks with cross-dressing, lobster racing, color-blind casting, and illicit love affairs, they allow us to view history through a new lens and feel surprisingly modern as a result. See our favorites below.

You can rely on Armando Iannucci to breathe new life into Charles Dickens’s sprawling bildungsroman. In the hands of the endlessly inventive comedian, the tale of a boy who pulls himself up by his bootstraps and seeks out fame and fortune becomes a madcap delight complete with a zingy script, cartoonish punch-ups, collapsing sets, and a heady dose of magical realism. Dev Patel is the dashing lead, supported by Peter Capaldi as a top-hatted menace and Tilda Swinton as an eccentric landowner who kicks trespassers off their donkeys.

highlights.title: Taika Waititi Says His Star Wars Movie Is 'on Ice'
highlights.summary: Director Taika Waititi has confirmed his long-in-development Star Wars movie is officially "on ice." The Thor: Ragnarok and Jojo Rabbit filmmaker provided Inverse with the update when speaking to the outlet during a press junket for his new film, Klara and the Sun.
body: "I hate to break this to you, but we're going to actually put it on ice and we're working on a different thing together," he said.

Brutal. Rumors that Disney and Lucasfilm had approached the What We Do in the Shadows filmmaker to helm a Star Wars project go as far back as January 2020. That's just a few years after he took off as the mastermind behind one of the most beloved Marvel Cinematic Universe movies to date, with an official announcement confirming he was attached to a movie arriving just a few months later.

It was mostly good news at first. In 2021, Waititi said he had finished his Star Wars movie's story, and in 2022, then-Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy said the goal was to bring it to theaters in late 2023. At the time, she also admitted that Disney hadn't "locked anything in" quite yet, a fact that only became more apparent in the years that followed.

highlights.title: There are five signs that someone dislikes you – but it’s best to ignore them | Polly Hudson
highlights.summary: All the possible indications, from eye contact to body language, come with a disclaimer. The truth is, you can never be totally sure... I’d be far less paranoid if everyone wasn’t out to get me, so when BBC Science Focus dangled “ The subtle signs somebody secretly dislikes you ”, I’ve never…
body: The first indication? They avoid eye contact. Apparently “someone who repeatedly looks away, scans the room or avoids mutual gaze might be creating psychological distance”. Agreed. But they may also be checking to see who else arrives, which might not mean they secretly hate you, only that they secretly don’t like you as much as whoever just came in.

The second sign is unarguably more convincing. “Their facial expressions show contempt or disgust.” Admittedly, I’m no psychologist, but still, if someone looked contemptuous or disgusted while interacting with me, I’d be pretty confident in concluding that they aren’t my greatest fan all on my own. File this one under bear/woods, pope/Catholic.

Third up, they “smile less around you”. This feels dangerous, because the only way to know whether they are smiling less around you than other humans they come into contact with is to put them under surveillance and keep a tally. If they didn’t dislike you before you hid in a bush counting their grins, they probably would afterwards.
